name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,661

clue.text: One blooming opiate isn't going astray!

indicators.note: things that go astray wander off their proper course, so the letters leave their order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved that their dose of a drug has not gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives POINSETTIA, the red-leaved Christmas plant; 'One blooming' is the definition, a cryptic way of saying a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A poinsettia is a seasonal plant sold for its showy flowering heads, so it is one thing that blooms.

clue.text: I sort out guy awaiting Yuletide gift delivery?

definitions.note: a first-person phrase standing for the noun: one who sorts out

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who puts things in order, speaking of themself
second meaning: a customer who has placed an order and waits for it to arrive

explanation.surface: A man tidying up while waiting for his Christmas parcels to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same word: one who arranges things tidily, and one who has placed an order.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -er makes an agent noun, so the word means both a person who arranges and a person who places an order with a shop.

clue.text: Daughter born close to Christmas conceals wants

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
to conceal is to hide something inside, so one piece goes within the others

blocks.note: née means born, used before a maiden name
standard abbreviation for daughter
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A baby girl arrives just before Christmas, and someone is keeping their wishes secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born close to Christmas' makes NEE + S, which hides the D for daughter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wants in the sense of necessities or requirements are needs, a straightforward synonym as plural nouns.

clue.text: English nurses hosting foremost of Xmas spreads

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is taken
a host takes a guest in, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
opening letter of the word
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: English nurses throw a Christmas party, laying out festive spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreads' looks like a noun for party food, but it is the verb. E + TENDS hosts the X after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread something out and to extend it both mean stretching it over a larger area, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A slice of roast topped with dash of table salt

a slice is only a small portion, here the first letter alone
in a down entry the topping sits above, so this piece is written first

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A slice of Christmas roast with a sprinkle of table salt on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' reads as seasoning, but an old salt is a sailor, as is a TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and tar are both informal nouns for a seaman, a crossword-favourite sense of each word.

clue.text: Slightly dry introduction to Laplander in a story

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
one group of letters is placed inside another

blocks.note: a story can be a lie, a fib; the A stays as written
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dull Lapland tale opens with a slightly dry introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly dry' wants to be one phrase, but the definition is 'Slightly' alone; 'dry' gives TT. TT + L goes into A LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To a small degree is what both mean, so the adverb and this two-word phrase swap in any sentence.

clue.text: Half-heartedly wed gal without IT experience

indicators.note: doing something with only half a heart loses part of the core, so one of the middle letters goes

blocks.note: to wed is to marry; one of its doubled central letters is dropped

explanation.surface: A reluctant bride marries a woman with no background in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' looks like computing, but here it means sex: the Virgin Mary conceived without it. MARRY loses one of its two central Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Nativity story the mother of Jesus is a virgin, so she is a woman with no sexual experience.

clue.text: I am one kind seen with right old lady in North Pole

definitions.note: the setter speaks of themself; the answer is the noun they are an example of

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another pair of letters

blocks.note: a mode is a kind or manner of something
standard abbreviation
compass abbreviation
informal for mother
N is one of the two magnetic poles

explanation.surface: Someone claims a kinship with Mrs Claus, the old lady at the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Pole' reads as Santa's home, but the two words are N and N, holding MA between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter, like every human living today, is a member of the present-day human species, so he counts as one.

clue.text: Wise man bearing note and bit of frankincense rolls joints

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it, so the other pieces are held inside
a bit is a small part, here just the opening letter
something that rolls over turns upside down, which in a down entry flips the order

blocks.note: a seer is a prophet or sage
the second note of the sol-fa scale
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: One of the Magi brings frankincense and some rolled-up cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the action of making joints, but it is the signal to turn the whole assembled string over, reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: American Express brought about Delta's arrival

indicators.note: to bring something about another is to put it around it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: A credit card company helped an airline's flight land.
explanation.walkthrough: American Express and Delta look like brand names; they are split into A, VENT and D, with A + VENT placed around D.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the coming of something, from the Latin for arrival, and gives its name to the weeks before Christmas.

clue.text: Shower expensive, but they say it's a beast!

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the letters follow the sound

blocks.note: a shower is rain and expensive is dear

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a costly new shower is a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like a bathroom fitting but is a fall of rain; 'dear' is the British sense of costly.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is a large antlered animal of the Arctic, so it is one kind of beast.

clue.text: Reporters covering hospital department awards

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it protects, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Journalists write up a hospital ward's prize ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awards' could be a noun, but it is the verb, matching PRESENTS as in 'presents a prize'.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone with a prize is formally to award it to them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Plonk with seconds upset men and son in post-roast states?

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, which in a down entry flips its order

blocks.note: to plonk something down is to put it
abbreviation for seconds
other ranks, ordinary soldiers
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Cheap wine and second helpings leave the family dazed after Christmas lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonk' looks like cheap wine but is the verb PUT. PUT + S turned over, then OR + S.
explanation.definitionFit: After a big roast dinner people fall into drowsy dazes, and a stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness.

clue.text: Flop in procreational period repelled legend

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so its letters run the other way

blocks.note: the rut is the mating season of deer
the legend on a map is its key

explanation.surface: A myth about failure during the breeding season.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird everyone expects at Christmas arrives via its slang sense: a turkey is a failed show or film.
explanation.definitionFit: In showbusiness slang a turkey is a production that fails badly, which is a flop.

clue.text: Fizzy Buds are ace accompaniment to a meal

indicators.note: fizzing things are agitated and bubbling, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fizzy Budweiser beers make a great drink with dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Buds are bottles of Budweiser beer, so the surface is about drinks. Bread sauce is a British sauce of milk thickened with breadcrumbs, served with roast turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread sauce is a traditional side served alongside Christmas roast poultry, so it accompanies the main course.

clue.text: Greeted in a Covid-safer way, say, by shaking raised ski

definitions.text: Greeted in a Covid-safer way, say

indicators.note: shaking jumbles contents, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A skier greets friends at a distance by waving a ski in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like an action of the ski, and 'shaking' like a handshake; both are just letters and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing the air beside someone's cheek avoids contact, so it is a greeting with less risk of spreading infection.

clue.text: Large amount of dope found on head of mission

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the opening letter is kept
one piece placed on another follows it in an across entry

blocks.note: first letter of the word
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A big drugs haul is discovered on the leader of a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' sets up drugs, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of something is a great quantity or heap of it, so the noun is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Sabbath singer making comeback as headliner

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters go back the way they came

blocks.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath
an informer sings to the police, and is called a rat

explanation.surface: The Black Sabbath frontman returns to top the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sabbath singer' evokes the rock band's vocalist; the words are split, and 'singer' is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: The headliner of a show is its main attraction, the performer billed at the top, its star.

clue.text: Airline trick raised Christmas hols each annum initially

indicators.note: lifting a word up a down entry makes it read bottom to top
what comes initially comes at the start, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: an art is a knack or trick
first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An airline pulls a fast one, hiking fares for holiday flights every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airline' looks like a carrier but means a passage for air, the windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube carrying breath down to the lungs, so it is literally a line for air.

clue.text: Hot to open new Foster's Special Reserve

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged
to open something is to get inside it, so one piece splits the other

blocks.note: something hot is fashionable, in
the brand taken as written, plus S for special

explanation.surface: A new special-reserve lager from the Foster's brewery is launched.
explanation.walkthrough: Foster's is an Australian lager brand. 'Reserve' looks like part of the beer's name; it means coolness of manner. IN goes into the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in a person is a cool, distant manner, and frostiness is an unfriendly chilliness of attitude.

clue.text: Father Christmas ultimately keeping one object for pals

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes last, so only the final letter is kept
to keep is to hold on to, so the outer pieces enclose the rest

blocks.note: abbreviation for a priest's title
the Roman numeral
an end is an aim or object
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Santa holds on to a single present meant for his mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Christmas' looks like Santa as one unit, but the two words are separate pieces: the priest's title and the last letter of the festive word, wrapped around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pals is the informal word for companions, people one likes and spends time with, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: 50% off tinsel brings in public with good advertising

indicators.note: taking half away leaves only the front portion of the word
to bring something in is to take it inside

blocks.note: the first half of the six letters
something made public is out in the open
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A half-price tinsel sale draws in shoppers thanks to clever adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public' looks like the noun for shoppers, but it is the adjective OUT, held inside the half of tinsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Touting is soliciting custom or promoting something persistently, much as advertising does.

clue.text: I'm told Jesus was one cold boy clothed in radiant light

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the spelling follows the sound

blocks.note: Jesus is called the Son of God
the tap abbreviation
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that baby Jesus was a chilly boy, wrapped up in a glowing light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jesus was one' points to SON, which sounds the same as SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means dressed, so to be dressed in the sun is to be wrapped in bright shining rays.

clue.text: Dick bringing Nina back sandwiches from Italy

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a name; it is slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Panini are toasted Italian bread rolls with fillings, so they are sandwiches of Italian origin.

clue.text: Uni fellows to stop member of Police jamming

explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' is capitalised because it is the rock band, not the force. 'Jamming' looks like playing music but means cramming.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamming something into a space means cramming or packing it in tightly, and stuffing means the same.

clue.text: Brother, fine with flipping wind, has third helping of sprouts

wind is moving air
third letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a sibling; it is a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of religious orders such as Franciscans address each other as Brother, and such a man is a friar.

clue.text: Very old crack found in strongbox by freak

explanation.surface: An ancient crack is discovered in a strongbox next to an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a split but means a joke; 'found in' links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a stale joke or story told too often, so a very old wisecrack.

clue.text: Those heading to icy emporium to get gift for Noel?

explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is the stereotypical present given to a man at Christmas, so it is one example of a gift.

clue.text: A drop of really cold water?

clue.text: Scoundrel pinching rear of our Queen?
